# Acts of Thomas — Chapter 8
**Agent:** EMET (Literal)
**Source:** Syriac MS / Greek recension, Acts of Thomas 8

---

*[The Eucharistic prayer. Thomas celebrates the sacrament with bread and water (no wine). The prayer over the oil. An extended liturgical section.]*

1. And when Thomas had baptized the many believers, he broke bread and gave thanks over it and said: "Come, O holy name of Christ that is above every name; come, power of the Most High and perfect mercy; come, thou highest gift; come, compassionate mother; come, thou that knowest the secrets of the Chosen One; come, thou that art in all the movements of the Chosen One; come, holy spirit, and purify their reins and their hearts and seal them in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit."

2. And when he had made this prayer, he broke the eucharist and gave a portion to each of them, saying: "Let this eucharist be unto you for life and forgiveness of sins and for the eternal resurrection."

3. And they said: "Amen."

4. And there was there a woman by name Mygdonia, who was the wife of Charisius, the kinsman of the king. And she saw Thomas and was greatly drawn to him.

5. And she pressed in among the crowd and stood beside him.

6. And Thomas saw her and said to her: "Who are you and what do you want?"

7. And she said: "I am Mygdonia, and I want to hear from you the word of life."

8. And Thomas said to her: "Blessed are you, Mygdonia, for you have sought what you need; for I will give you the living water that quenches all thirst, and bread of heaven that satisfies all hunger."

9. And he gave her the eucharist and she received it with joy.

10. And when it was night, Thomas took oil and poured it over his head and began to pray and said: "Come, holy name of Christ; come, power of the Most High; come, gift of the Most High; come, compassionate father; come, fellowship of the male; come, revealer of the hidden mysteries; come, mother of the seven houses, whose rest was in the eighth house; come, elder of the five members — intelligence, thought, prudence, reflection, reasoning — communicate with these young men."

11. And after he had poured the oil, he prayed over those who were present and said: "Let the mercy of the Holy Spirit come and rest upon them."

---
*EMET note: The Eucharist here is celebrated with bread and water — no wine. This is characteristic of early Syriac Christianity and certain encratite communities. The invocation of the Holy Spirit as "compassionate mother" (*'em raḥmana*) reflects Syriac Christian theology, where the Spirit is grammatically feminine and associated with motherhood.*
